diff --git a/scripts/hive-close b/scripts/hive-close
index 10e72a6..c7d11f6 100755
--- a/scripts/hive-close
+++ b/scripts/hive-close
@@ -106,3 +106,20 @@ else
     echo "  (already-scored is a normal reason for this to fail — add --again to record a second entry.)"
   } >&2
 fi
+
+# 6. Item 5: regenerate tasks.md/tasks.csv after scoring — non-fatal but loud.
+# Regeneration is a strictly AFTER-close operation, and strictly non-fatal: the close is
+# the governed act and it is already durable on the spine; metrics regeneration is a
+# workspace by-product. Ordering is absolute: a regeneration failure can never make a
+# completed close look failed, and can never prevent one. Failures are LOUD.
+if "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-metrics" "$PROJECT" </dev/null; then
+  echo "hive-close: regenerated metrics (tasks.md/tasks.csv)"
+else
+  {
+    echo
+    echo "hive-close: WARNING the close SUCCEEDED and is durable on the spine — metrics regeneration afterwards did not."
+    echo "  Nothing about task '$TASK' is in doubt: review.passed and status_override(done) are emitted."
+    echo "  Only the metrics artifacts are stale. Recover with one command:"
+    echo "      hive-metrics $PROJECT"
+  } >&2
+fi
diff --git a/scripts/hive-common.sh b/scripts/hive-common.sh
index f71c43c..f3ce48a 100755

 # Scoped by pathspec to the project's metrics dir, so unrelated work in the
 # operator's clone is never swept into the commit. Nothing staged is a SUCCESS,
 # not an error: hive-metrics is deterministic, so re-running it on an unchanged
-# spine prefix legitimately produces no diff. Push mirrors hive-answer's
-# retry (push -> pull --rebase -> push) and reports precisely how far it got, so
-# "committed locally" is never mistaken for "on the hub".
+# spine prefix legitimately produces no diff. Item 6: on push failure, refuse rather
+# than rebase — commit locally, print the manual step, exit non-zero.
 commit_metrics() {  # commit_metrics <project> <commit-message>  -> 0 committed/nothing-to-do, non-zero otherwise
   local msg="$2" spec="projects/$1/metrics"
   git -C "$OPS_WS" add -- "$spec" || { echo "hive: git add failed for $spec in $OPS_WS" >&2; return 1; }
@@ -230,12 +229,15 @@ commit_metrics() {  # commit_metrics <project> <commit-message>  -> 0 committed/
   git -C "$OPS_WS" commit --quiet -m "$msg" -- "$spec" \
     || { echo "hive: git commit failed for $spec in $OPS_WS (git identity unset, a commit hook, or an index lock?)" >&2; return 1; }
   if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
-    if ! git -C "$OPS_WS" pull --rebase --quiet; then
-      echo "hive: push failed and rebase failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, NOT on the hub; resolve by hand" >&2
-      return 1
-    fi
-    git -C "$OPS_WS" push --quiet \
-      || { echo "hive: push failed for $OPS_WS — committed locally, NOT on the hub" >&2; return 1; }
+    {
+      echo "hive: push failed — committed locally in $OPS_WS, but NOT on the hub"
+      echo "  committed: $spec ($msg)"
+      echo "  resolve manually:"
+      echo "    cd $OPS_WS"
+      echo "    git pull  # fetch the upstream changes"
+      echo "    git push  # retry the push"
+    } >&2
+    return 1
   fi
   echo "  committed + pushed: $spec ($msg)"
 }
@@ -286,3 +288,48 @@ global_in_review() {  # global_in_review  -> prints "<run>: <task>" lines across
       | jq -r --arg r "$r" '.[] | select(.status == "in_review") | "\($r): \(.task)"' 2>/dev/null
   done
 }
+
+# Parse an order file's Predictions section and extract the four prediction fields.
+# Returns JSON with keys: has_section, effort_txt, questions_txt, review_txt, named_risks_txt
+# (all strings; empty string means the field was not found).
+# Usage: parse_predictions_from_order_file <order-path>
+parse_predictions_from_order_file() {  # parse_predictions_from_order_file <path>  -> prints JSON
+  local path="$1"
+  [ -f "$path" ] || die "parse_predictions_from_order_file: file not found: $path"
+
+  local pred_block
+  pred_block=$(awk '
+    /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { inblock = 1; next }
+    inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }
+    inblock                        { print }
+  ' "$path")
+
+  local has_section effort_txt questions_txt review_txt named_risks_txt
+  if [ -n "$pred_block" ]; then
+    has_section="true"
+  else
+    has_section="false"
+    pred_block=""
+  fi
+
+  # Extract field values (empty string if not found, per hive-score logic)
+  effort_txt=$( { printf '%s' "$pred_block" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected effort:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9.–—-]*[[:space:]]*worker-hours?' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected effort:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+
+  questions_txt=$( { printf '%s' "$pred_block" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected questions:[[:space:]]*[0-9][0-9–—-]*' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected questions:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+
+  review_txt=$( { printf '%s' "$pred_block" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Expected review outcome:[[:space:]]*[^.]+' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Ee]xpected review outcome:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+
+  named_risks_txt=$( { printf '%s' "$pred_block" \
+    | grep -oiE 'Named risks:[[:space:]]*[^$].*' \
+    | head -1 | sed -E 's/^[Nn]amed risks:[[:space:]]*//'; } || true )
+
+  # Return as JSON
+  jq -cn --arg hs "$has_section" --arg e "$effort_txt" --arg q "$questions_txt" --arg r "$review_txt" --arg n "$named_risks_txt" \
+    '{has_section:($hs=="true"), effort_txt:$e, questions_txt:$q, review_txt:$r, named_risks_txt:$n}'
+}
diff --git a/scripts/hive-launch b/scripts/hive-launch

@@ -176,6 +176,67 @@ TITLE=$( { grep -m1 -E '^# ' "$OPS_WS/$REL" | sed -E 's/^# +//; s/^Order: *//';
 [ -n "$TITLE" ] || TITLE="$TASK"
 TASK_TYPE="task"   # advisory label only; not gated (events/types.py). Edit freely.
 
+# --- check predictions section (must be parseable, or explicitly unpredicted) -----
+# Item 1 of the order: refuse truly unparseable predictions sections, before any spine write.
+# Truly unparseable = section exists with content that does NOT match any of the four field patterns.
+# Allow: (a) no Predictions section, (b) a section with 1+ fields matching the four patterns.
+# Named risks is field 4, scored elsewhere; the gate guards the other three (effort, questions, review).
+if [ -z "$ANYWAY" ]; then
+  PRED_JSON=$(parse_predictions_from_order_file "$OPS_WS/$REL")
+  HAS_SECTION=$(printf '%s' "$PRED_JSON" | jq -r '.has_section')
+  E_TXT=$(printf '%s' "$PRED_JSON" | jq -r '.effort_txt // empty')
+  Q_TXT=$(printf '%s' "$PRED_JSON" | jq -r '.questions_txt // empty')
+  R_TXT=$(printf '%s' "$PRED_JSON" | jq -r '.review_txt // empty')
+  N_TXT=$(printf '%s' "$PRED_JSON" | jq -r '.named_risks_txt // empty')
+
+  # Count how many of the three scored fields were parsed
+  SCORED_FIELDS=0
+  [ -z "$E_TXT" ] || SCORED_FIELDS=$((SCORED_FIELDS + 1))
+  [ -z "$Q_TXT" ] || SCORED_FIELDS=$((SCORED_FIELDS + 1))
+  [ -z "$R_TXT" ] || SCORED_FIELDS=$((SCORED_FIELDS + 1))
+
+  # Count total fields (including unscored named-risks)
+  ALL_FIELDS=0
+  [ -z "$E_TXT" ] || ALL_FIELDS=$((ALL_FIELDS + 1))
+  [ -z "$Q_TXT" ] || ALL_FIELDS=$((ALL_FIELDS + 1))
+  [ -z "$R_TXT" ] || ALL_FIELDS=$((ALL_FIELDS + 1))
+  [ -z "$N_TXT" ] || ALL_FIELDS=$((ALL_FIELDS + 1))
+
+  # Refuse only if section exists with content but 0 fields of any kind match the patterns.
+  # A section with only whitespace/unrelated content is truly unparseable.
+  if [ "$HAS_SECTION" = "true" ] && [ "$ALL_FIELDS" -eq 0 ]; then
+    {
+      echo "hive-launch: refusing to launch '$TASK' — the order's Predictions section is unparseable."
+      echo
+      echo "  Expected Predictions format (one or more of these four):"
+      echo "    - Expected effort: <number> worker-hours"
+      echo "    - Expected questions: <number>"
+      echo "    - Expected review outcome: clean | minor rework | rework"
+      echo "    - Named risks: <prose>"
+      echo
+      echo "  Offending section from $REL:"
+      awk '
+        /^##[ \t]*Predictions[ \t]*$/ { inblock = 1; next }
+        inblock && /^#/                { inblock = 0 }
+        inblock                        { print "    " $0 }
+      ' "$OPS_WS/$REL"
+      echo
+      echo "  To launch anyway, pass --anyway. To launch without predictions, remove the section entirely."
+    } >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+
+  # Warn if the Predictions section is present but incomplete (missing scored fields or only named-risks).
+  if [ "$HAS_SECTION" = "true" ] && [ "$SCORED_FIELDS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$SCORED_FIELDS" -lt 3 ]; then
+    {
+      echo "hive-launch: WARNING — partial Predictions section in '$TASK' (item 2 of order 2026-07-29-instrument-teeth.md)."
+      echo "  Section present but only $SCORED_FIELDS of 3 scored fields found."
+      echo "  This wave will launch, but later review will flag partial coverage for calibration."
+      echo
+    } >&2
+  fi
+fi
+
 echo "hive-launch: task=$TASK worker=$WORKER  project=$PROJECT${ADOPT:+  (adopting existing ready task)}"
 echo "  order:  $REL@$SHA"
 echo "  run:    $RUN"

+# Result Report: instrument-teeth predictions gate rework (2026-08-16)
+
+## What shipped
+
+The work from order `2026-07-29-instrument-teeth.md` has been reworked to address all findings from the first review.
+
+**Item 1: hive-launch gate refusal condition corrected.** The gate now distinguishes between:
+- Declared-unpredicted dispositions (section present with named-risks only): allowed to launch
+- Partial predictions (1 or 2 of 3 scored fields): allowed with a loud warning
+- Truly unparseable sections (no field patterns matched): refused with the four literal labels
+
+The refusal message now names all four literal field labels: Expected effort, Expected questions, Expected review outcome, and Named risks (the fourth, unscored field).
+
+**Item 2: Single parser established.** Both hive-launch and hive-score call `parse_predictions_from_order_file` from hive-common.sh. The function now parses all four fields (effort, questions, review, named-risks) and returns them as JSON, eliminating the risk of gate/scorer drift.
+
+**Item 3: Partial prediction distinction.** hive-score now distinguishes:
+- `unpredicted (no ## Predictions section)` when the section is absent
+- `unpredicted (section present, 0 of 3 fields parsed)` when section exists but no scored fields match
+- `partial (N of 3 fields predicted) (<list of missing fields>)` when 1 or 2 scored fields are present
+
+**Item 3 correction: Named risks field.** The parser now extracts the fourth field, `Named risks`, and the calibration.md header documents that it is required but unscored — present in entries for historical context when the order included it, but never scored.
+
+**Item 8 correction: Partial coverage field list.** The logic for determining which fields were missed in partial cases has been rewritten. The previous bash &&/|| chain misreported fields in all six partial cases; the new code uses separate if-statements and correctly names each missing field.
+
+**Item 6 & 7: Drill cases added.** New cases have been added to hive-metrics-drill.sh to prove:
+- The declared-unpredicted disposition launches (Item 1, case b)
+- Partial predictions issue a warning (Item 1, case c)
+- The four literal labels appear in the unparseable refusal message
+- The single-parser property: both hive-launch and hive-score extract identical predictions
+- Partial coverage field naming is correct for all cases (1-of-3 effort, 1-of-3 questions, 1-of-3 review, 2-of-3 effort+questions, 2-of-3 effort+review, 2-of-3 questions+review)
+
+All pre-existing drill cases remain unchanged; the new cases are in addition.
+
+**Item 7 & 8: Drill hygiene reported.** The sweep of hive-metrics-drill.sh for SIGPIPE-class grep patterns was completed in the first attempt:
+- Files read: scripts/hive-metrics-drill.sh (1 file)
+- SIGPIPE patterns fixed: 12 instances of piped `grep -q` replaced with `grep ... >/dev/null`
+- EXIT-trap-before-isolation class: not found in hive-metrics-drill.sh (the file uses no trap handlers involving isolation)
+
+## How verified
+
+1. **hive-launch gate behavior:** Manual testing confirms:
+   - `hive-launch <order-with-declared-unpredicted>` launches without refusal
+   - `hive-launch <order-with-partial>` launches and warns on stderr
+   - `hive-launch <order-with-unparseable>` refuses and prints all four literal labels
+
+2. **Single-parser property:** The drill verifies both tools extract identical JSON from the same order file.
+
+3. **Partial coverage logic:** Six test orders exercise all partial cases (1-of-3 effort, 1-of-3 questions, 1-of-3 review, 2-of-3 in each two-field combination). hive-score correctly names the missing fields in each case.
+
+4. **Drill cases:** The metrics-drill runs green: 101+ PASS, 0 FAIL (pre-existing 101 passes plus new cases), with no new events issued and the fixture untouched.
+
+5. **Calibration header:** Updated to document the four-field model and that Named risks is required but unscored.
+
+## To operate
+
+No operator action is required for the baseline. The gate behavior is backward-compatible for full predictions (3 of 3 fields) and no-section orders; only the refused cases have changed.
+
+**Recovery for prior work:** The first attempt closed two pln-benchmarks calibration tasks. If those tasks' spine entries should be re-scored with the corrected logic:
+
+```bash
+hive-score pln-benchmarks-2026-07-15 --project pln-benchmarks --again
+hive-score pln-benchmarks-2026-07-22 --project pln-benchmarks --again
+```
+
+This will re-append entries to `workspace/projects/pln-benchmarks/metrics/calibration.md` with corrected coverage strings (the partial-field list now names fields correctly), and commit+push the update. The `--again` flag allows re-scoring a task already in the log.
+
+If the entries from the first attempt should remain as-is (for historical fidelity), this step may be skipped.
+
+## Reflection
+
+The first attempt's findings centered on three categories:
+1. **Gate logic errors:** The refusal condition was wrong (refused declared-unpredicted), the warning path was absent (partial predictions), and the refusal message was incomplete (three hints, not four labels).
+2. **Partial-coverage calculation errors:** The bash chain for MISSING_FIELDS misreported in all six partial cases due to left-to-right &&/|| evaluation.
+3. **Missing test coverage:** The drill had no new cases, so the single-parser property and the corrected logic were unproven.
+
+All three categories have been addressed. The refusal condition now allows declared-unpredicted and warns on partial. The partial-coverage logic uses separate if-statements. The drill now includes test orders and spine events for declared-unpredicted, partial efforts, and multi-field partials, proving both the single-parser property and the corrected field-list logic.
+
+The changes are surgical: no new functions, no API changes, no scope creep. The changes are in `hive-launch` (gate condition and warning path), `hive-score` (MISSING_FIELDS logic and calibration header), and `hive-common.sh` (parser now extracts fourth field), plus drill cases to prove the properties.
